**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve swapchain memory before advertising bind_memory2**

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Withhold driver_properties until driverID is valid**

Advertising `VK_KHR_driver_properties` makes `VkPhysicalDeviceDriverProperties` queryable, but `r300vk_physical_device_init_properties` deliberately returns `driverID = (VkDriverId)0` even though the local Vulkan registry/header define `VkDriverId` values starting at 1 and mark this returned member as an exact limit. Any app or CTS case querying the newly exposed extension now observes an out-of-enum driver ID, so either a valid Mesa driver ID needs to be used or this extension should remain hidden.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Don't advertise StorageBuffer SPIR-V that graphics rejects**

With `VK_KHR_storage_buffer_storage_class` enabled, a graphics shader may use an SSBO declared with the SPIR-V `StorageBuffer` storage class, but the r300vk graphics compile path still rejects every `vulkan_resource_index` whose descriptor type is not `nir_descriptor_type_uniform_buffer` in `r300vk_nir_lower_vulkan_resource_index_single`. Such pipelines now fail at create time despite the extension being advertised, so keep this hidden until the StorageBuffer descriptor path is actually accepted for the advertised shader stages.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor alias images before exposing bind_memory2**

`VK_KHR_bind_memory2` also exposes `VK_IMAGE_CREATE_ALIAS_BIT_KHR`, but r300vk never inspects image create flags: `r300vk_CreateImage` allocates a fresh Gallium resource for each image, and `r300vk_BindImageMemory2` only points the memory object back at that already-created image resource. An app that enables this extension and creates two alias images bound to the same memory range will therefore get two independent resources instead of shared backing storage.

When `R300_R2VB_MVP_SINGLECS=1` is tested together with `R300_R2VB_BARRIER=nozb`/`norb`/`nowait`, this second hard-coded barrier still emits the ZB/RB flushes and wait even though `r300_r2vb_emit_producer` explicitly lets that env var neuter those pieces for timing bisection. That makes the single-CS probe results misleading because the supposedly disabled barrier component is immediately reintroduced before the draw; factor the same masked values into this re-asserted barrier or apply the same gate here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reassert the barrier before LOAD_VBPNTR**

In the single-CS path this barrier runs after `r300_prepare_for_rendering(... PREP_EMIT_VARRAYS ...)`, so the helper has already emitted `3D_LOAD_VBPNTR` for the redirected clip buffer; for non-indexed draws that packet is sent with `R300_VC_FORCE_PREFETCH`, which can start the vertex fetch before these cache/VAP flushes execute. That leaves the stale-fetch race this patch is trying to close for any hardware that prefetches on LOAD_VBPNTR, so the barrier needs to be placed before emitting the vertex-array packet or the LOAD_VBPNTR must be re-emitted after the barrier.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Propagate computed-varying re-ingest failure**

When `R300_R2VB_REINGEST=1` and the new hard gate refuses a shape (for example `num_attribs != 2`) or `r300_r2vb_exec_passthrough_draw()` fails, this call's `false` result is ignored and the surrounding block still returns `true` to `r300_swtcl_draw_vbo`, which skips the gallivm `draw_vbo` fallback. That makes unsupported or failed computed-varying re-ingest cases drop the draw instead of falling back after the documented refusal; the re-ingest result needs to decide whether this path can claim the draw was handled.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Delete the cached producer VS before destroying draw**

On SWTCL contexts `r300_delete_vs_state()` calls `draw_delete_vertex_shader(r300->draw, ...)` (and may also unbind from `r300->draw` if the CSO is still bound), but `r300_destroy_context()` has already destroyed `r300->draw` a few lines above. Once `r300_r2vb_get_producer_vs()` has lazily built this cached VS, context teardown can therefore call into a freed draw module; delete the cached producer VS before `draw_destroy()` or avoid the draw-dependent delete path after teardown.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove the task label from the source comment**

`AGENTS.md` says source comments must not cite internal issue/task numbers or review chronology, and `#1a` is a task label rather than a hardware/API mechanism that a Mesa maintainer can verify later. Please replace this with the actual mechanism being scoped here (for example, producer-only BO oracle before re-ingest wiring) or remove the label.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fall back when varying producer setup fails**

With `R300_R2VB_VARYING=1`, a failure to build the re-staged FS or allocate the varying BO skips this whole producer block, but the enclosing `vslot >= 0` path still cleans up and returns `true`, so `r300_swtcl_draw_vbo` suppresses the gallivm fallback even though no varying was produced or re-ingested. Treat `!vfs || !vbo` as an unhandled draw and return `false` after cleanup so allocation/compile failures do not silently drop the draw.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Dirty vertex arrays after restoring producer BO slots**

After a successful computed-varying re-ingest, `r300_r2vb_exec_passthrough_draw()` has emitted `LOAD_VBPNTR` for the temporary `clip`/`vbo` slots and can clear `vertex_arrays_dirty`; restoring the original vertex elements and buffers here without marking the arrays dirty leaves a later direct-VB/R2VB draw able to reuse the stale producer-BO arrays after those resources are released. Mark `r300->vertex_arrays_dirty` when restoring this temporary vertex state, just as real vertex-buffer changes do.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use American English in new comments**

`AGENTS.md` requires American English spelling in new or modified source comments, but this added comment uses `colour`; the same spelling appears in other added R2VB comments as well. Please use `color` consistently so the patch follows the repository's documented comment style.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject non-contiguous position inputs**

When a restaged VS computes `gl_Position` from two attributes that are not the first two vertex elements, this loop still copies `velem[0]` and `velem[1]` into the producer. The re-stager maps the surviving NIR input variables to `VAR0`, `VAR1`, etc. in shader input order, so a shader using, for example, attributes 0 and 2 will be accepted by `count_position_inputs()==2` but `VAR1` receives vertex element 1 instead of attribute 2, producing the wrong clip BO/re-ingest result. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Coalesce split VA H.264 start-code buffers**

When the VA frontend receives H.264 slice data without an Annex-B start code, `handleVASliceDataBufferType` appends the 3-byte start code as its own buffer before the slice bytes (`src/gallium/frontends/va/decode.c:217-222`), and `vlVaEndPicture` forwards that buffer array unchanged. This loop treats every buffer as a complete slice NAL, so common VA clients that omit start codes will decode a start-code-only “slice” and then a start-code-less slice once a provider is enabled; coalesce adjacent start-code/data buffers or parse the concatenated bitstream before calling the provider.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use real H.264 slice types**

When H.264 is enabled, this writes the video profile enum (for example `PIPE_VIDEO_PROFILE_MPEG4_AVC_CONSTRAINED_BASELINE`) into `vl_h264_slice_contract.slice_type`, whose contract enum is P/B/I/SP/SI. The VA H.264 path stores the actual per-slice values in `pipe_h264_picture_desc.slice_parameter.slice_type[]`, so any provider or back half that consults this frame field will see an out-of-range profile value and make slice/picture decisions from the wrong domain.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve provider decode failures**

Once a provider is available, unsupported H.264 features or malformed slice data can make `decode_slice` return false, but this loop discards that result and allows `end_frame` to proceed with partially populated or zeroed macroblock records. That turns a fail-closed provider error into corrupted output for the current frame; store a decoder error state and have `end_frame` fail or skip emission when any slice decode fails.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep H.264 hidden until the back half renders**

If a CPU VLD provider is added before the FP24 back half, `r300_h264_decode_available()` will start advertising H.264, but this `end_frame` path still returns success without writing the target surface. In that staged environment VA clients would get successful decode calls with stale or blank frames, so the availability gate needs to include back-half readiness or this function must fail closed until it actually emits the frame.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require the exact experimental opt-in**

This experimental decoder gate uses Mesa's generic boolean parser, which accepts values such as `yes`, `true`, and `y`; the repository's AGENTS.md requires hazardous/experimental opt-ins to accept only the exact value `1` and reject all other unset, empty, zero, or non-exact values. Use a string comparison against `"1"` here so accidentally permissive environment values do not enable the H.264 path once a provider is present.

When the replay contract is not a dense frame starting at macroblock 0, such as a sliced capture whose first record has a nonzero `mb_x`/`mb_y` or records from a larger frame, this `memcpy` writes record `i` into `out->macroblocks[i]`. The provider interface requires decoded records to land at their raster index, and the comment above says out-of-frame records are ignored; this instead shifts or truncates macroblocks and feeds the back half the wrong coefficients and motion vectors. That contradicts the public contract in `vl_h264_contract_wire.h` that failure leaves `slice` untouched, and can leave a reused slice with old `macroblocks` but new dimensions/provider metadata. When this render-to-texture test is used to validate the transform's exact integer result, rounding `got[i]` before comparing masks fractional shader errors up to half a unit even though the comment says every expected value is f32-exact at zero tolerance. **suggestion:** The 4x4 block scan tables and xy_to_blk helper are duplicated across modules

These blk_x/blk_y tables and `xy_to_blk` are identical to those in `vl_h264_mb_decode.c`. Please factor them into a shared helper/header so both prediction and residual traversal use the same mapping and stay in sync, which will also ease future extensions (e.g., explicit 8x8 support).

Suggested implementation:

```c
#include "vl_h264_cavlc.h"
#include "vl_h264_cavlc_residual.h"
#include "vl_h264_scan.h"

```

```c
/*
 * Clean-room from ITU-T H.264 sec 7.3.5.3 (residual traversal) and 9.2.1 (the nC
 * neighbour derivation).  No third-party decoder source was consulted.
 */

/* A neighbour macroblock is available when it is inside the frame, in the same
 * slice, and already decoded (raster order). */
static bool

```

To fully factor out the shared scan tables and helper:

1. Add a new header, e.g. `src/gallium/auxiliary/vl/vl_h264_scan.h`:
   - Declare the tables and helper as:
     - `extern const uint8_t vl_h264_blk_x[16];`
     - `extern const uint8_t vl_h264_blk_y[16];`
     - `unsigned vl_h264_xy_to_blk(unsigned bx, unsigned by);`
   - Optionally move the existing comment about sec 6.4.3 into this header.
2. Add a new implementation file, e.g. `src/gallium/auxiliary/vl/vl_h264_scan.c`:
   - Define the tables and helper (removing `static` and using the new `vl_h264_`-prefixed names):
     - `const uint8_t vl_h264_blk_x[16] = { ... };`
     - `const uint8_t vl_h264_blk_y[16] = { ... };`
     - Implement `vl_h264_xy_to_blk` with the same loop currently used in `xy_to_blk`.
3. Update this file and `src/gallium/auxiliary/vl/vl_h264_mb_decode.c` (and any other users) to:
   - Include `"vl_h264_scan.h"`.
   - Replace uses of `blk_x`/`blk_y` with `vl_h264_blk_x`/`vl_h264_blk_y`.
   - Replace calls to `xy_to_blk` with `vl_h264_xy_to_blk`.
4. Ensure the new `vl_h264_scan.c` is added to the appropriate build system files so it is compiled and linked into the Gallium auxiliary library.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle CAVLC level escape prefixes**

For valid CAVLC residuals that use the escape path (`level_prefix >= 16`, which occurs with large coefficient levels), this only gives the 12-bit suffix to prefix 15 and then computes `level_prefix << suffixLength` directly. H.264 9.2.2 requires the suffix size to grow as `level_prefix - 3`, uses `min(15, level_prefix)` in the base code, and adds the escape offset for prefixes >=16; otherwise the decoder leaves escape suffix bits unread and desynchronizes the rest of the block/slice.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Correct high-end chroma QP mapping**

When `qPI = qp_y + offset` is 44, 46, or 47, this table returns QPc values one step too high (`38, 39, 39`), while H.264 Table 8-15 maps those inputs to `37, 38, 38`. Any stream that drives chroma QP into that range (high luma QP or positive chroma offset) will publish the wrong `qp_cb`/`qp_cr`, so chroma dequant/deblock uses a different quantizer from the bitstream and bit-exact decode fails.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Load oracle fields as little-endian**

On big-endian runners, the committed oracle file remains little-endian (record 0 has bytes `01 00 00 00` for `mb_type`), but copying it into a host `int32_t` turns it into `0x01000000`, so this predicate never recognizes I_NxN blocks and the test fails at `checked_i_nxn > 0`; the dequant test repeats the same host-endian interpretation for `int16_t` coefficients. Please decode the oracle fields with explicit little-endian loads.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep CAVLC table generation repo-local**

This generated header points maintainers at a `steinmarder` script outside the Mesa checkout for regeneration, but the root `AGENTS.md` requires Mesa source, test, upstream-sync, and submission flows to remain independent of `steinmarder`. As written, a Mesa-only update to the spec tables cannot reproduce or audit this generated file; please move the generator/provenance into this repo or replace the comment with a Mesa-relative regeneration path.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mark intra blocks with unused references**

For the new I-slice path, `ref_l0` and `ref_l1` are never initialized to the contract's `-1 = not used` value, so zeroed CAVLC records look like inter blocks with reference 0. The deblock code classifies intra edges only when both reference lists are negative (`deblock_strength` in `vl_h264_emit.c`), so every CAVLC-produced intra macroblock gets inter boundary strengths instead of the required intra strengths; please set both ref arrays to -1 when filling an intra macroblock contract.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Copy slice deblock controls into each contract**

When the slice header signals `disable_deblocking_filter_idc == 1` or nonzero alpha/beta offsets, this decoder never copies those parsed `dec->slice` fields into the macroblock contract. The new tests zero `mb`, so CAVLC-produced records reach `vl_h264_emit_deblock_luma/chroma` with filtering enabled and offsets 0 regardless of the bitstream, producing the wrong post-deblock picture for those valid slices.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid left-shifting negative coefficients**

A kernel with 33+ `ffloor` ops therefore passes the 64-op test here while exceeding the R300 64-ALU hardware program limit, so the producer can run dummy/wrong code and consume the draw under the R2VB exec/reingest gates instead of falling back; please count `ffloor` as two emitted slots or validate the compiled program before accepting it.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle extended CAVLC level prefixes**

For conforming streams that encode a large residual level with `level_prefix >= 16`, this path reads the wrong suffix width and computes the wrong `levelCode`: H.264 §9.2.2 uses `levelSuffixSize = level_prefix - 3`, `Min(15, level_prefix)`, and an extra `(1 << (level_prefix - 3)) - 4096` term (see https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-H.264). As written, those coefficients are decoded to much smaller values and the bitstream is also desynchronized for prefixes above 15, so high-residual CAVLC blocks corrupt the decoded macroblock.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Correct the high chroma QP remap entries**

For macroblocks where `qp_y + chroma_qp_index_offset` lands on 44, 46, or 47, this table returns QPC values one step too high compared with the H.264 QPC mapping table (44 should map to 37, and 46/47 should map to 38; see https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-H.264). That makes the native CAVLC path over-dequantize chroma at those QPs, producing color-plane coefficient mismatches even when luma decoding is correct.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject CABAC PPS before CAVLC decode**

When the active PPS has `entropy_coding_mode_flag == 1`, this still accepts ordinary I/P slices based only on `slice_type`, but the macroblock/residual path added here always calls the CAVLC readers rather than the CABAC `ae(v)` syntax required by H.264. A Main/High-profile CABAC stream would therefore be parsed as if it were CAVLC and produce corrupted macroblocks instead of failing closed; the slice parser should reject non-CAVLC PPS state before handing the reader to the CAVLC front end.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Consume the 8x8-transform flag for I_NxN**

When `pps->transform_8x8_mode_flag` is set for an I_NxN macroblock, H.264 §7.3.5 inserts `transform_size_8x8_flag` immediately after `mb_pred` and before `coded_block_pattern` (see https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-H.264). This branch goes straight from `decode_intra4x4_pred` to the CBP path without consuming or rejecting that bit, so High-profile CAVLC I_NxN macroblocks are parsed one bit off and the residual/QP fields that follow are corrupted.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Account for separate colour plane IDs**

When `sps->separate_colour_plane_flag` is set, H.264 §7.3.3 adds a 2-bit `colour_plane_id` between `pic_parameter_set_id` and `frame_num` (see https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-H.264). This parser only notes that Constrained Baseline lacks the field and immediately reads `frame_num`, so a valid CAVLC separate-plane slice is shifted by two bits instead of being rejected before macroblock decode.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject or parse multi-reference P syntax**

For valid Baseline P slices where the PPS or slice override makes `num_ref_idx_l0_active > 1`, H.264 codes `ref_idx_l0` before the motion-vector differences for these partitions. This decoder reads the MVD immediately and hardcodes `ref_l0` to 0, so multi-reference streams go out of bitstream sync and point at the wrong reference instead of being rejected as out of scope; gate on the parsed `dec->slice->num_ref_idx_l0_active` before decoding partitions or consume the reference indices.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject CABAC PPS before CAVLC parsing**

When `entropy_coding_mode_flag` is 1, P/B slice headers include `cabac_init_idc` and the macroblock residuals are CABAC-coded, but the existing slice parser never consumes `cabac_init_idc` and the new macroblock path always uses CAVLC readers. Accepting this PPS therefore causes CABAC streams to be parsed out of bit alignment instead of being rejected as outside the Constrained-Baseline/CAVLC front-end scope.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject PPS 8x8 transform mode until parsed**

If a High-profile PPS sets `transform_8x8_mode_flag`, the macroblock layer can carry `transform_size_8x8_flag` and luma residuals use the 8x8 transform path, but the new macroblock decoder always sets `mb->transform_8x8 = 0` and never consumes that syntax element. Accepting such a PPS lets valid 8x8-transform streams desynchronize at the first affected macroblock; reject this flag until the macroblock and residual paths implement it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject separate colour planes when parsing SPS**

For High 4:4:4 streams with `separate_colour_plane_flag` set, the slice header contains `colour_plane_id` after `pic_parameter_set_id`, but `vl_h264_parse_slice_header()` explicitly skips that field and the residual path only handles non-separate 4:2:0 chroma. Storing the flag and still returning success means those unsupported streams are accepted and then parsed out of bit alignment; return false here when the flag is set, matching the header contract.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject high-bit-depth SPS before 8-bit decode**

When a High-profile SPS advertises 10/12-bit video here, parsing still succeeds even though the macroblock and dequant paths hard-code the 8-bit QP domain, including modulo-52 QP wrapping and the 8-bit chroma QP table. Such a stream will be decoded with the wrong quantization rules rather than being rejected as outside this 8-bit CAVLC front-end scope; reject nonzero bit-depth offsets before exposing the SPS.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject interlaced SPS before frame-only decoding**

If `frame_mbs_only_flag` is 0, this parser accepts field/MBAFF streams, but the slice-header object drops `field_pic_flag` and the macroblock loops/neighbour availability operate in simple frame raster order. Those interlaced streams will therefore use the wrong macroblock count and neighbour topology instead of failing early; reject non-frame-only SPS until the downstream decoder retains and handles field state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject weighted P prediction until weights are retained**

When `weighted_pred_flag` is set for a P slice, the slice parser only consumes the prediction weight table and discards the weights, while the new inter contract carries only refs and MVs. Any downstream motion compensation will therefore be unweighted and reconstruct the wrong pixels for weighted P streams; reject this PPS flag until the weights are preserved in the slice/contract and applied.
